title: Derived morphisms from an arbitrary K-projective complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a chosen derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ in the universe convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ for the category of integer cochain complexes modulo chain homotopy and $Q_h:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Here a chain homotopy from $f$ to $g$ is a family $h^n:P^n\to E^{n-1}$ with $f-g=d_Eh+hd_P$. Call a complex $P$ K-projective if, for every acyclic complex $N$ (zero cohomology in every degree), every chain map $P\to N$ is chain homotopic to zero. For every K-projective $P$ and every complex $E$, the canonical map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(P,E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(Q_hP,Q_hE)$$
is bijective. No boundedness or termwise projectivity hypothesis is imposed on $P$.
